Wiktionary ( US : / ˈ w ɪ k ʃ ə n ɛr i / ⓘ WIK -shə-nerr-ee , UK : / ˈ w ɪ k ʃ ən ər i / ⓘ WIK -shə-nər-ee ; rhyming with "dictionary") is a multilingual, web -based project to create a free content dictionary of terms (including words , phrases , proverbs , linguistic reconstructions , etc.) in a large number of natural languages and a number of artificial languages . These entries may contain definitions , images for illustration, pronunciations , etymologies , inflections , usage examples, quotations , related terms, and translations of terms into other languages, among other features. It is collaboratively edited by volunteers via a wiki . Its name is a portmanteau of the words wiki and dictionary . It is available in 198 languages and in Simple English . Like its sister project Wikipedia , Wiktionary is run by the Wikimedia Foundation , and is written collaboratively by volunteers , dubbed "Wiktionarians". Its wiki software , MediaWiki , allows almost anyone with access to the website to create and edit entries.
